newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BONDS HOLD LOW LEVELS, AWAIT MORE U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BONDS HOLD LOW LEVELS, AWAIT MORE U.S. DATA.

text.p: Belgian bonds were stuck at their initial depressed levels on Thursday after stronger-than-expected U.S. retail sales and weekly jobs data sent Treasuries lower.

"We've got producer prices and consumer price data ahead. Nobody wants to go short now for the coming days," one dealer said. February U.S. PPI figures are due on Friday, to be followed by consumer prices next Wednesday.
By 1530 GMT the 10-year OLO yield was 5.81 percent, above the previous close of 5.77, though just below 5.82 percent touched earlier.
"I see the spread narrowing to seven or eight basis points next week," he added, saying there were no domestic factors to justify a spread widening.
OLO yields at the shorter end of the curve were little changed from the previous day's higher levels, though there was a fair amount of activity noted in two year paper.
Front-month bond futures stood 0.22 point lower at 121.78.

Short-term money market yields were seen remaining high, with the National Bank squeezing liquidity. Three-month T-bills were at 3.47/57 percent, up from 3.46/50 a day ago. -- Lorrayne Smith, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6812, Fax +32 2 230 7710
